questions.explain: Confident wrongness, silent model decay, automation bias, data leakage into models, and unbounded action space are the five named failure modes, and every control in the chapter traces back to one of them.
options: Confident wrongness, silent model decay, automation bias, data leakage into models, and unbounded action space
Slow queries, deadlocks, blocking, fragmentation, and log growth
High CPU, memory pressure, disk latency, network timeouts, and failed backups
Missing indexes, stale statistics, bad plans, parameter sniffing, and implicit conversions
questions.q: Which five failure modes of AI in database operations does the chapter name?

questions.explain: The four required fields are the evidence snapshot, the model version, the reasoning trace, and the counterfactual threshold — without them, an action was not explainable and should not have run autonomously.
options: The DBA's name, the server name, the database name, and the time of day
The LLM's token count, the prompt length, the API cost, and the response latency
The evidence snapshot, model version, reasoning trace, and the threshold the decision crossed
The incident ticket number, the change request ID, the CAB approval date, and the rollback window
questions.q: What four fields must the automation audit log capture for every AI-driven action to satisfy the chapter's explainability bar?

questions.explain: Tier 3 rows carry min_confidence 1.01, which no model output can ever reach, making autonomous execution of failovers and schema changes structurally impossible rather than merely discouraged.
options: They require two human approvers instead of one
They carry an unreachable confidence threshold (1.01) so the executor can never clear them autonomously
They are only allowed to run during maintenance windows
They require the kill switch to be enabled first
questions.q: How does the oversight tier registry guarantee that Tier 3 actions (failover, schema changes) can never run autonomously?

questions.explain: Literal redaction strips string and numeric literals so the model sees query shapes rather than customer data, and egress allowlisting restricts the automation host to approved model endpoints.
options: Encrypting the model weights with Always Encrypted
Running the LLM on the database server itself
Requiring DBAs to review every prompt by hand
Redacting literals from SQL text before it enters LLM context, and allowlisting which model endpoints the automation host may call
questions.q: What two technical controls does the chapter recommend for governing what data flows into AI systems?

questions.explain: The four steps are: flip the kill switch to halt autonomous execution, reconstruct the timeline from the explainability log, roll back to the last known good, and run a blameless review that produces one structural control change.
options: Delete the automation logs, retrain the model immediately, and resume execution
Page the vendor, wait for a patch, and keep the system halted indefinitely
Halt via the kill switch, reconstruct from the explainability log, roll back, and fix the failed control structurally
Blame the on-call engineer and disable all AI systems permanently
questions.q: What is the chapter's four-step incident response when automation causes an outage?
